title: microbooks for interdimensional traveling
content:
tactile portals for jumping through my creative multiverse
see also: tiny circles as completion fuel

I want to share a breakthrough tool in my own creative systems and infrastructures — the microbook, as tiny, focused containers for navigating my creative landscape. they act as tactile portals into my obsessions and ideas, bypass inertia and perfectionism, and help me move between creative domains, with lightness and ease.

what you see above is a spread of microbooks I made, in a sudden burst of electric energy, one sunday afternoon, while I was teaching creative systems — from which this idea emerged. each book represents a capsule-sized exploration into a specific topic, theme, or process in my creative life and business. my first microbook was actually this field notes about my systems.

I’ll explain how I’m thinking about the microbook as a form — and why it’s been so groundbreaking for me.

microbook vs. zine — a spontaneous, tiny book

I’ve played with the handmade book / zine as form before — I made this sleep zine a few years ago, this meditation booklet in 2018, this chapbook/booklet of tango essays in 2019, and more recently, a digital zine on deconstructing the productivity machine.

when I heard that the zine form was experiencing a resurgence in popularity recently, I won’t lie, it first triggered an instinct for me to run in the other direction. instead, I thought a bit about the zine as a pure creative form — independent of its history with different subcultures, its DIY publishing and distribution ethos, or its present day appeal in the era of Substack / social media fatigue.

what is a zine, as a distilled form?
what appeals to me about it?
what can I use it for?

the answer I found was — I’m interested in the form as a container for creative process, where the pages can be written in an ongoing way, or in a sudden flash of inspiration, with minimum effort and inertia. because books feel usually so laborious to create, I’m most interested in the “zine” form — because it suggests a tiny, spontaneous book.

   

an ongoing vessel for process

I’m interested in how the spontaneous book form meets my creative consciousness, my relationship to process, time, and practice.

I am actually not that interested (at least right now) in its ease of distribution, making photocopies, selling my zines, doing zine swaps, zine community-building, or even the zine as a vessel for sharing my work.

I realize that my approach to this creative form — very much like my approach to websites as world-building — is solitary, internal, and forever ongoing, moving through iterations, layerings, and rebirths.

before I even think about other people seeing my work, I make my books for me. I make them to think through something, with my hands, on paper.

it’s more about the process — than a concrete output.
it’s more of an ongoing journal — than a miniature magazine.
it’s more like a stack of sequential sticky notes — than a creative “thing.”
it’s more of a place for my meandering thoughts, loosely stitched together.

it’s throwaway, it’s tiny, it can be thrown together in 10 minutes, forgotten about and remade again, in iterative cycles, from scratch.

I felt like word “zine” carried too many connotations for me — and I wanted to engage with it, purely, as a piece of paper — much like I engage with the website as an imaginary world, rather than a digital brochure.

so that’s how I came up with my own word an conceptual framing — microbook.

   

boundaried depth & infinite expansion

I use the form of a microbook as a tiny, analog container for shaping, holding, and working with my creative process. it’s a tool for making the immaterial and imaginative feel more concrete and contained. each microbook feels like tiny material cups into which I can pour from my creative essence / star energy.

then, whenever I run out of pages, I just glue another booklet to the back of one to add more pages. I’ve been using the single sheet, 8 page zine fold, but you can use any type of booklet fold.

a microbook is both boundaried (limited by the size of the pages / 8 pages) — and infinite, elastic, and expandable — like an accordian.

the boundaries give it a concise clarity of form. it allows me to go deep into one topic or obsession — I close the book, and then I’ll open it back up again, to remember what I was thinking about.

each microbook feels like a portal into a rabbit hole in my mind; immediately transportable. I can keep falling down the hole, or I can jump holes.

modularity & tiny completions

sometimes I make a microbook in one day (like the tax therapy microbook or the systems field notes) — and it helps me think through a single difficult task or project with more presence, and clarity. it feels like a talisman to help me stay perceptive and aware, to integrate the experience, write down what I learned, and refer to again in practice.

other times, a microbook will be indefinitely ongoing (like my ideas microbook), or, it will accompany me over a specific window of time. during my trip to China, I made 2 microbooks (see photos above) with the intention of filling out 1 page in each per day.

the green book = what happened each day
the red book = how I felt about it

this structure allowed me to be both comprehensive and consistent in my daily practice — and it was a small enough container (taking 5-10 minutes) that I encountered very little resistance to working on it.

this is an example of my tiny circles concept in practice, and of working in what I’m calling micro-practices — units of time so small as to instigate very little resistance.

   

microbooks as portals & space

I start with folding the paper and naming the book — setting an intention for it, as a clear creative container.

for example, I showed my partner K all of my microbooks, and he says, “what about going on adventures with us?” so I took a pre-folded book and drew his and Luna’s face on the cover, and named it “K & L Adventures” (see photo above), and I intend to fill it with a diary of things we did together, places we go, or the places we want to go together.

the act of opening a microbook container is to make space for what you value in your life.

I make microbook containers for whatever I want to think more about, dream more of, cultivate more of, or tend to, more of, in my life.

it is an act of giving care, attention, and ongoing practice to whatever I hold as precious, or whatever inspiration sparkle I’m captivated by, even if just for a moment. it is a vessel to hold dreams, a potted container to give form to seedling visions, or, a pocket talisman to remind me of who I am, when I’m lost in some wormhole or time loop. it is both a door for me to walk through, and a keyhole to take me home.
